description: The customer's town is found via invoice line → order item → order → customer.

a.request: Link each invoice line item to its order through its order item (`Order_Items.order_id`), and from the order to the customer's town or city. First, for each order item id and town, average the line `product_price` and the ratio `derived_product_cost` / `derived_total_cost`, ignoring missing values. Then, for each town, average those per-item averages. Show the towns whose average cost ratio is above the average of that ratio across all towns, with the town, its average price, its average ratio, and how much its ratio exceeds the cross-town average. No rounding.
a.sql:
WITH per_item AS (
  SELECT
    o.customer_id,
    oli.order_item_id,
    AVG(oli.product_price) AS avg_item_price,
    AVG(CAST(oli.derived_product_cost AS REAL) / NULLIF(oli.derived_total_cost, 0)) AS avg_item_cost_ratio
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items AS oli
  JOIN Order_Items AS oi ON oi.order_item_id = oli.order_item_id
  JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  GROUP BY o.customer_id, oli.order_item_id
), per_town AS (
  SELECT
    c.town_city,
    AVG(pi.avg_item_price) AS average_price,
    AVG(pi.avg_item_cost_ratio) AS average_cost_ratio
  FROM per_item AS pi
  JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = pi.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.town_city
), town_baseline AS (
  SELECT AVG(average_cost_ratio) AS cross_town_average_ratio
  FROM per_town
)
SELECT
  pt.town_city AS town,
  pt.average_price,
  pt.average_cost_ratio,
  pt.average_cost_ratio - tb.cross_town_average_ratio AS ratio_excess
FROM per_town AS pt
CROSS JOIN town_baseline AS tb
WHERE pt.average_cost_ratio > tb.cross_town_average_ratio;

c.request: Using the town or city of the customer who placed the order behind each invoice line item: first, for each order item id and town, average the line `product_price` and the ratio `derived_product_cost` / `derived_total_cost`, ignoring missing values; then average those per town. Which towns have an average cost ratio above the average across all towns? Show the town, its average price, its average ratio, and how far its ratio is above the cross-town average, without rounding. The customer's town is found via invoice line → order item → order → customer.
c.sql:
WITH item_town_averages AS (
    SELECT
        oi.order_item_id,
        c.town_city,
        AVG(ili.product_price) AS avg_product_price,
        AVG(ili.derived_product_cost / NULLIF(ili.derived_total_cost, 0)) AS avg_cost_ratio
    FROM Invoice_Line_Items AS ili
    JOIN Order_Items AS oi ON oi.order_item_id = ili.order_item_id
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY oi.order_item_id, c.town_city
), town_averages AS (
    SELECT
        town_city,
        AVG(avg_product_price) AS avg_price,
        AVG(avg_cost_ratio) AS avg_ratio
    FROM item_town_averages
    GROUP BY town_city
), cross_town_average AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio
    FROM town_averages
)
SELECT
    t.town_city,
    t.avg_price,
    t.avg_ratio,
    t.avg_ratio - x.avg_ratio AS ratio_above_cross_town_average
FROM town_averages AS t
CROSS JOIN cross_town_average AS x
WHERE t.avg_ratio > x.avg_ratio;

b.request: Compute average `product_price` and `derived_product_cost / derived_total_cost` for each `(order_item_id, customer town)` across invoice line items, ignoring missing values; then average those per town. Return towns whose average ratio exceeds the unweighted average of the town averages, with town, average price, average ratio, and the difference from that cross-town average, without rounding
b.sql:
WITH item_town AS (
    SELECT
        ili.order_item_id,
        c.town_city AS town,
        AVG(ili.product_price) AS avg_price,
        AVG(1.0 * ili.derived_product_cost / NULLIF(ili.derived_total_cost, 0)) AS avg_ratio
    FROM Invoice_Line_Items AS ili
    JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.invoice_number = ili.invoice_number
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, c.town_city
), town_averages AS (
    SELECT
        town,
        AVG(avg_price) AS average_price,
        AVG(avg_ratio) AS average_ratio
    FROM item_town
    GROUP BY town
), cross_town AS (
    SELECT AVG(average_ratio) AS cross_town_average_ratio
    FROM town_averages
)
SELECT
    ta.town,
    ta.average_price,
    ta.average_ratio,
    ta.average_ratio - ct.cross_town_average_ratio AS difference_from_cross_town_average
FROM town_averages AS ta
CROSS JOIN cross_town AS ct
WHERE ta.average_ratio > ct.cross_town_average_ratio;

d.request: Using the customer town associated with each invoice line item through the invoice line → order item → order → customer relationship, calculate for each order item and town the average `product_price` and the average ratio `derived_product_cost / derived_total_cost`, ignoring missing values. Then average those values by town. Which towns have an average cost ratio above the average across all towns? Show each town’s average price, average cost ratio, and the difference between its ratio and the cross-town average, without rounding.
d.sql:
WITH order_item_town_averages AS (
  SELECT
    c.town_city,
    oli.order_item_id,
    AVG(ili.product_price) AS average_price,
    AVG(ili.derived_product_cost / NULLIF(ili.derived_total_cost, 0)) AS average_cost_ratio
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items AS ili
  JOIN Order_Items AS oli
    ON ili.order_item_id = oli.order_item_id
  JOIN Orders AS o
    ON oli.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN Customers AS c
    ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.town_city, oli.order_item_id
), town_averages AS (
  SELECT
    town_city,
    AVG(average_price) AS average_price,
    AVG(average_cost_ratio) AS average_cost_ratio
  FROM order_item_town_averages
  GROUP BY town_city
), overall_average AS (
  SELECT AVG(average_cost_ratio) AS average_cost_ratio
  FROM town_averages
)
SELECT
  t.town_city,
  t.average_price,
  t.average_cost_ratio,
  t.average_cost_ratio - a.average_cost_ratio AS difference_from_cross_town_average
FROM town_averages AS t
CROSS JOIN overall_average AS a
WHERE t.average_cost_ratio > a.average_cost_ratio;
